title: Two reproducible atlases, one basin research portal
scope: Pskem pilot first, then all 7,445 native level-12 basins in the Amu Darya and Syr Darya systems. Coarser nested levels are derived views, not additional independent basins.
recommendation: Proceed with basin-level temporal storage and staged expansion. Maintain static layers by source release and time-varying layers by complete observation period. Preserve source-native information; do not upsample every variable to a common fine grid.

stages.title: Attach HydroATLAS reference attributes to basins
stages.description: Keep the original 281-attribute baseline attached to native level-12 HYBAS_IDs, with source descriptions, units and local/upstream support. Attachment is complete; independent reproduction is a separate requirement.
deliverables: Versioned reference values and basin geometry
Explicit joins at the correct basin level
Original values available in the basin modal
stages.gate: Original values and missing values preserved; no pilot-to-region copying or accidental joins between nested basin levels.

stages.title: Update HydroATLAS substitutes: pilot, benchmark, region
stages.description: The 20-unit Pskem run has 196 substitutes and 34 original-source candidates. Expose the saved estimates in a separate modal tab; develop dated adapters and resumable batches before regional execution.
deliverables: Updated substitutes tab; light green only for an available value on the exact basin
Pilot dated precipitation, temperature, water balance and snow with QA counts
Representative 100–250 basin benchmark across both systems
Resumable regional source/period batches and regional coverage ledger
stages.gate: Stage 5 storage contract adopted (done: every new value enters through the observation store); pilot method review, source completeness, units, topology and retry/idempotency tests pass before expanding. Report pending families instead of inventing substitutes.

stages.title: Reimplement the Uzbekistan environmental atlas
stages.description: Use the existing 134-package national environmental inventory to catalogue each theme's original method, source, scale, legend and period. Reimplement one thematic module in Pskem, validate it, then apply the same batching contract to the two river systems.
deliverables: Environmental-atlas theme-to-source/method crosswalk; include unavailable inputs and licence limits
Pilot environmental indicators linked to basin observations
Reviewed batches for Amu Darya and Syr Darya
Separate exact reimplementations, alternative-source estimates and non-comparable indicators
stages.gate: Resolve source methods and units, validate one complete thematic pilot, retain local/upstream support and run an independent reproduction. Compare to national reference only where that reference has coverage; transboundary transfer requires separate validation.

stages.title: Publish research and accessible basin data
stages.description: The local portal already serves maps, pilot evidence and downloads. Extend it to reviewed regional editions, dated basin series, methodological comparisons and reproducible research packages.
deliverables: Basin tabs for original and substitute evidence, period selector when real dated records exist
CSV/Parquet tables, versioned geometry, metadata and frozen run manifests
Citable research pages and reproducible analysis notebooks/scripts
Public deployment, licensing checks and accessible downloads
stages.gate: Browser and download checks, explicit missing/QA states, consistent snapshot IDs and a clean-environment rerun. Local publication does not imply public deployment or peer review.

stages.title: Preserve time, resolution and research opportunities
stages.description: The observation/revision contract is adopted and executable: ATLAS_MODULES/core/observations.py is the only way into the store. It holds 10,735,860 rows, of which 10,725,600 are dated monthly observations of six variables covering every one of the 7445 level-12 basins from 2003 to 2022, beside the frozen HydroATLAS run's static values, source epochs and climatologies. Each value carries its source release, method, geometry and QA denominators; 11,814 are null and say why. The production physical design and revision traffic from real corrections remain open.
deliverables: Append-only basin observation/revision store with source, method, geometry and run identities
Distinct observation period, retrieval time and publication time
Native spatial resolution, processing grid, basin support, cadence and completeness beside every value
Spatial/temporal opportunity flags in attribute tables; never equate a flag with an achieved improvement
stages.gate: Round-trip a frozen snapshot, append a corrected month without losing the earlier version, preserve nulls and distinguish monthly observations from monthly climatologies. Reject mixed units, changed geometry or period definitions in an unversioned series.

stages.title: Report changes, monitor anomalies and connect the ontology
stages.description: After both atlas methods and temporal records are reviewed, run scheduled source checks, thematic comparisons and anomaly reporting. Extend the existing ontology with evidence-linked observations and research findings.
deliverables: Thematic difference reports with source/method-change attribution
Seasonal anomaly series against pinned baselines and independently checked events
Source freshness, incomplete-period and failed-batch monitoring
Reviewed links among basin, observed property, source, method, observation, run and finding
stages.gate: A source or sensor change cannot silently become an environmental-change claim. Anomalies require comparable units/methods, complete-period rules, baseline/sample counts and declared thresholds; ontology assertions cite evidence and carry review status.

next_batches: Explain the source-availability trend in the dated snow record before any snow trend is published from it: null basin-months roughly triple from 2003 to 2022 while daily source image counts stay constant, and from 2006 they reach basins of several hundred cells rather than only the smallest. Until it is explained, a change in what the sensor delivered cannot be told apart from a change in the snow.
Date the remaining time-varying family, surface water inundation, which needs the JRC Monthly History asset and its own method review rather than a change of parameter.
Reproduce one pilot attribute independently, in a second environment, against pinned inputs. Nothing in the programme has cleared reproduction gate 6 and every stage above assumes it.
Add a second dated family through the same path, so the store holds more than one time series and the observation contract is exercised by a variable with different masking behaviour.
Expand by source × period × spatial batch with bounded concurrency, checkpoints, hashes, idempotent retries and a regional completeness ledger.
Repeat the validated process for the first environmental-atlas thematic module before adding the other themes.

storage_contract.status: Adopted for staging in ATLAS_MODULES/core/observations.py, which enforces it on every record; existing static run CSVs are retained. The production physical design stays open.
storage_contract.implementation: The executable field names follow the long table specified in ATLAS_MODULES/core/REPRODUCIBILITY.md, which is the single authority; the groupings below describe the same record. Staged to PUBLISHED/data/atlas/observations/ as CSV partitioned by time kind, with versioned run, recipe, source-release and basin-geometry tables beside it.
storage_contract.physical_design: Versioned basin/source/method/run tables plus partitioned long observations (year/source family), indexed by basin/indicator/period. Start with portable Parquet and a query engine or PostgreSQL/PostGIS; benchmark the choice before production. Raster evidence stays in source/tile/period storage with checksums, not duplicated per basin.
storage_contract.ontology_mapping: Proposed mapping: basin as feature of interest, indicator as observed property, dated value as observation, method as procedure, source snapshot as provenance entity and extraction run as provenance activity. Keep numeric arrays in the observation store and link them from the ontology. Semantic mappings require review.

runtime.regional_grouped_kernel_note: Projection of 250 reductions from a full-domain synthetic arithmetic benchmark. This is not an implemented end-to-end atlas runtime, source download time or scientific validation.
runtime.baseline_interpretation: The regional reduction is no longer the constraint: one grouped pass over the full 7,445-basin 15 arc-second frame takes 0.51 seconds, so a 250-pass run is about 2.1 minutes, against 14.3 hours for the per-basin scan it replaced. Loading and rasterising the frame costs 4.1 and 1.0 seconds once per run. Acquisition is now the dominant cost and depends on the source; the ~18.5-hour raster-download projection still stands for adapters that download rasters, while the server-side reduction path avoids that download entirely.
runtime.incremental_interpretation: Measured on 250 representative basins across both systems: twelve months of MODIS snow reduced on the server in 16.7 seconds cold, returning 2968 values in 351 KB with no raster downloaded. Extrapolated linearly that is about 0.7 minutes for one month across all 7,445 basins and about 2.8 hours for a full twenty-year monthly series. Earth Engine does not scale linearly under quota, queueing or retry, and a repeated benchmark inherits its cache, so these are planning allowances rather than delivery times.
runtime.environmental_interpretation: No runtime estimate yet for the environmental atlas. Each theme needs input/method discovery and a pilot benchmark; HydroATLAS source timings do not transfer automatically.
runtime.storage_note: Same footprint/band-count raw raster scaling only. Native 3 arc-second processing requires about 25× as many cells as 15 arc-seconds; 1 arc-second requires 225×. Do not upsample coarse climate data. Basin tables stay one row per basin/indicator/period.
runtime.regional_current_reduction_note: Superseded by measurement. The 17.6-hour figure extrapolated the per-basin scan; measuring that same scan on the real 7,445-basin frame gives 14.3 hours, and the grouped pass that replaced it gives 2.1 minutes for the same 250 reduction passes.
runtime.regional_monthly_series_note: Measured, not extrapolated: 1,786,800 rows for 7445 basins over 2003-2022, in 2.25 hours with no failed batch and no retry. The 2.8-hour figure beside it was the linear extrapolation from the 250-basin sample, and it was about 23% high.
runtime.regional_dated_note: Three sources, six dated attributes, every one of the 7,445 basins for 2003-2022: 10,720,800 rows in 5.91 hours of extraction with no failed batch and no retry in any run. Band stacking is why: reducing over basin geometry costs about the same for six bands as for one, so TerraClimate delivered four variables in less time than MODIS took for one.

publication_rules: Original HydroATLAS values are immutable reference evidence. Substitute availability is highlighted light green, including valid zeroes, only for the exact basin and run.
Green is not an accuracy, temporal recency or independent-validation badge. Missing substitutes stay uncoloured and explicit.
Future spatial/temporal improvements are outlined research flags with reasons, not claims that new detail has already been obtained.
Every published edition links source metadata, methods, executable code, environment, checksums, geometry and review outcomes so another researcher can reproduce it.
